reuse.why: Step 0 is done well (getDateWithWeekendRule now takes the skip flag and every caller routes through it), but later steps do not reuse it consistently: holidays are threaded only from getNextDate and the daily skip is re-coded in getDatesInRange.

duplication.why: The weekend-move logic is single, but the daily-skip decision exists twice in different shapes (a retry loop in getNextDate and an inline null-return in getDatesInRange).

placement.why: The move rule and isNonWorkingDay sit in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip decision is split between shared getNextDate and the server handler instead of a shared definition.

scope.why: Changes stay within the schedule weekend/holiday feature and the new handler; the rename of getDateWithSkippedWeekend is part of the requested refactor.

maintainability.why: Callers apply different subsets of the rule: getUpcomingDates and the budget template ignore holidays and daily skipping, getDatesInRange skips weekends but not holidays, and getNextDate has an unbounded while(true) loop, so the rule will drift further.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) re-implements daily skipping with d.isWeekend and no holidays; getUpcomingDates and budget/schedule-template.ts call getDateWithWeekendRule without holidays and without the daily-skip rule

disguised_duplication.where: daily skip appears as a retry loop over isNonWorkingDay in getNextDate and as a reshaped `daily && skipWeekend && isWeekend -> null` map branch in getDatesInRange

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithWeekendRule gains skipWeekend and holidays; getNextDate gains a daily-skip loop; getDatesInRange reimplements it while getUpcomingDates and schedule-template.ts omit holidays and daily skipping
